title: OpenAI invoke arbitration + fragmented message serializer for deterministic tool selection
author: Sasha Ortega
description:
Motivation: Downstream customers reported two classes of incompatibilities when proxying OpenAI-style function/tool calls through Redwood: (1) nondeterministic 'tool_choice' semantics under temperature/sampling when multiple compatible tools exist, and (2) fragmented streaming messages for long, structured tool outputs that break standard JSON schema validators. This PR implements a compatibility layer that (a) introduces an arbitration step to normalize tool_choice semantics to deterministic, policy-driven selection while preserving sampling behavior when explicitly requested, and (b) replaces the previous naive streaming envelope with a FragmentedMessageSerializer that emits framed, schema-aware fragments plus finalization markers to safely reconstruct structured outputs on clients that expect either OpenAI streaming frames or Redwood framed envelopes.

Summary of changes: single-continuous description of the work below.

Design highlights:
- Arbitration: add invoke_arbitrator that sits before tool invocation. By default it deterministically selects the highest-priority tool based on model-intent matching and explicit tool annotations (preferred, fallback). If the original request included sampling semantics (temperature > 0 and top_k/top_p present) the arbitrator emits a selection token in the streaming path instead of forcing a fully deterministic pick; clients can opt-in to either strict-deterministic or permissive-sampling modes via the new 'invoke_selection_mode' parameter (values: "deterministic", "sample-allow").
- Serializer: FragmentedMessageSerializer splits structured outputs (large JSON blobs or newline-delimited JSON) into schema-bound fragments. Each fragment includes a compact header: {fragment_id, seq, total_estimate, schema_tag}. A finalization frame contains the canonical schema_hash and a CRC of the reconstructed payload to aid client-side validation. Serializer supports both OpenAI-style data: and tool invocation frames and Redwood's internal framed envelope; we map between them based on client compatibility hints.
- Backwards compatibility: default behavior matches previous Redwood semantics for existing clients. OpenAI-compat clients (detected via Accept-Compat header or compatibility flag in request) receive framing that mirrors OpenAI streaming boundaries while preserving the fragment headers in a hidden metadata channel (x-rw-frag) so proxies can reconstruct.
- Runtime: minimal overhead assigned to fast-path: small, in-place headerization for fragments and a predict-first-run policy that avoids recomputing model->tool match scores where a cached profile exists.

Testing & rollout plan:
- Added unit tests for arbitration deterministic vs sampling modes (tests/api/test_invoke_arbitrator.py).
- Integration tests cover streaming reconstruction under simulated network reordering, truncated frames, and client-side schema validation failures (tests/integration/test_fragmented_stream_roundtrip.py).
- E2E perf microbenchmarks show median added overhead < 1ms per fragment for typical 8k-token outputs on GPU nodes; regression tests added to perf-canary harness.
- Rollout: enable on staging for 48h behind feature flag rw:openai-invoke-compat, then ramp to 10% production, monitor tool-invoke error rate and invocation latency percentiles.

Why this is different from prior work:
- We explicitly separate selection policy (arbitration) from execution: previously selection was implicit in the sampling loop and hard to reproduce. The arbitration API is pluggable for future rules (cost-aware, region-aware, ML-based selector) without changing streaming framing.
- The serializer provides a formalized fragment header and finalization CRC which prevents silent schema corruption that customers reported during ephemeral reconnects.

Risks / mitigations:
- Clients that depend on raw token streams might need minor updates: mitigated by dual-path framing and automatic downgrading to legacy stream for clients that pass no-compat headers.
- Edge-case: model-initiated tool handoffs (multi-tool chains) require arbitration to be reentrant. We added reentrant-safe locks and idempotency keys to prevent duplicated invocations.

Checklist:
- [x] implement arbitration logic and serializer
- [x] unit + integration tests
- [x] docs (redwood-docs/compatibility/invoke.md) updated with selection_mode and fragment schema
- [x] perf canary
- [x] feature flag gated rollout plan

Notes: the description above is the single string for the PR body. See commits for more granular step notes.
commits: 6 commits: 1) introduce invoke_arbitrator + tests; 2) add FragmentedMessageSerializer core implementation; 3) wire serializer into streaming runtime and OpenAI compat adapter; 4) integration tests for reconstruction & reordering; 5) perf optimizations for header allocation; 6) docs + changelog
review_comments: Marcus: Can the arbitration step be configured per-route via console? Response (Sasha): yes — added route-level config and Console UI hooks; Lina: serializer header size might add overhead in small fragments, can we compress header? Response: switched to 8-byte compact header and delta-encoded seq which reduced header overhead by ~36%; Evan: tests look good but add a case for truncated finalization CRC fail -> added test and handling to emit explicit 'schema_mismatch' exit frame before connection close.
release_notes: Add deterministic invoke arbitration and a schema-aware fragmented streaming serializer for OpenAI compatibility. Introduces request parameter 'invoke_selection_mode' and feature-flag rw:openai-invoke-compat. Backwards-compatible by default.
notes_for_ops: Feature flag rw:openai-invoke-compat is disabled by default. To enable: set feature flag per-tenant in Console or via /admin/features. Monitor metrics: invoke.failure_rate, streaming.fragment_reconstruct_success, invoke.latency_p50/p99. Rollback: disable flag; serializer is not forced on legacy clients.
changelog_entry: compat: deterministic invoke arbitration + fragmented message serializer (OpenAI invoke compatibility).
